Delphina Brings Total Funding to $15M to Take Trusted AI Analytics from the Data Team to the CEO's Office
News provided by
Delphina Inc.
Nov 12, 2026, 10:01 ET
Share this article
Share this article
Radical Ventures and Costanoa double down as Delphina launches the Context Factory, where AI agents build and maintain the business context behind trusted answers
SAN FRANCISCO , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Delphina , whose Context Factory uses AI agents to build and maintain the business context behind trusted AI analytics, announced $7.5 million in new funding, bringing its total funding to $15 million. The round was co-led by Radical Ventures and Costanoa, with participation from Tenacity Capital joining high-profile angels Fei-Fei Li, Nobel laureate Guido Imbens, and early employees of Anthropic and OpenAI. . Delphina will use the funding to scale the Context Factory and grow its go-to-market and customer engineering teams.
Delphina was built to meet data teams' standards, but business teams now ask 73% of the questions on the platform, and CEOs at more than half of its customers are active users. At Substack, more than 70% of employees use Delphina, including CEO Chris Best. Other customers include LATAM Airlines, Gen Digital, Upstart, Udemy, Medely, Coursera, and BaseCamp Franchising.
"We want to give our people superpowers with AI. Delphina does that for data," said Chris Best, CEO of Substack. "Now our teams get accurate answers in seconds instead of waiting weeks in a queue. It's changed how we make decisions."
AI analytics is only as good as what it knows about the business: which tables are trusted, how metrics are defined, and what experienced analysts know but never wrote down. Most companies build that context by hand, and it goes stale as the business changes. The Context Factory hands that work to agents. They build a working baseline from a company's existing data and documents in hours, find and fix gaps as people ask questions, and route important changes to domain experts for approval.
"At Uber, everyone, including the CEO, was hands-on with data. That direct line to the numbers was a real advantage, but it took an army of data engineers to keep it from collapsing into chaos," said Jeremy Hermann, Delphina's CEO and co-founder. "The Context Factory gives every company that same advantage. Agents do the heavy lifting, and data teams become the knowledge captains who decide how the business sees its numbers."
"Most companies are data-obsessed but struggle to become data-driven," said Duncan Gilchrist, Delphina's President and co-founder. "When everyone can get trusted answers, everyone suddenly has questions. Ops, sales, marketing and finance teams are now the heaviest users of Delphina, and they keep coming back."
Hermann built and led Uber's Michelangelo machine learning platform and co-founded Tecton, which was acquired by Databricks. Gilchrist led global pricing data science at Uber. The Context Factory is available today at delphina.ai .
About Delphina
Delphina gives everyone in a company, from the front line to the CEO, trusted answers from the company's own data. Its Context Factory uses AI agents to build and maintain the business knowledge that enables accurate AI analytics, with experts approving important changes. Delphina is based in San Francisco and backed by Radical Ventures and Costanoa Ventures. Learn more at delphina.ai .

AI Mental Health Startup Siggy Launches With $6 Mn in Pre-Seed Funding
Global Digital Health News
Story By DHN Bureau
•
1 day ago
•
3 Mins Read
•
Last Updated On : 11 Nov 2026
Siggy aims to deliver personalized mental health care through a system that integrates human clinicians with AI tools for patient intake and support between appointments.
AI-enabled virtual mental health provider Siggy has launched out of stealth with $6 million in pre-seed funding to develop a continuous care platform combining therapy, prescription management and AI-powered patient support. The startup is backed by Village Global and several angel investors.
Siggy aims to deliver personalized mental health care through a system that integrates human clinicians with AI tools for patient intake and support between appointments. Its intake process is free, and patients pay only if they choose to proceed with treatment.
Patients begin with a free, anonymous conversation with Siggy’s AI, without requiring an account or login. The system retains their history, allowing them to avoid repeating information when they consult a provider. An AI-powered preliminary diagnosis is reviewed by clinicians, who then present treatment options.
After an initial call with a human provider, patients can log in to add existing providers or relatives to the system and confirm their treatment goals. Those who accept treatment meet a human clinician monthly and can engage with Siggy’s AI between visits.
The AI therapy agent draws on patients’ full histories to help them work through treatment goals, recall prescribed exercises and discuss their progress. It does not answer medical questions and directs patients to human providers for clinical guidance. Safety protocols are also in place to flag patients with higher-acuity needs to clinicians.
Siggy also connects with wearables and offers a one-minute daily check-in covering sleep, mood, physical well-being, and medication side effects. These inputs contribute to a daily Siggy Score, measured on a scale of 0 to 100 and visible to both patients and clinicians. The platform flags emerging patterns to clinicians, while weekly check-ins during the first two months allow providers to assess whether medication doses should be maintained, increased or changed.
“It can build a really detailed picture of you rather fast, and the idea is if there are behavior patterns that are recurrent…[Siggy can] begin to help people gain agency and recognize them before they happen,” Siggy co-founder and CEO Jonathan Sabbagh told Fierce Healthcare.
Sabbagh co-founded the company with Edvard Engesaeth, M.D., who serves as COO and previously co-founded Nurx. Daniel Montville, M.D., a Mayo Clinic-trained psychiatrist, is the company’s chief medical officer. Sabbagh previously spent two decades in finance before pursuing psychology and co-founding Journey Clinical, a US-based psychedelic-assisted therapy network.
The launch comes amid challenges with continuity in mental health treatment. About 16% of American adults take antidepressants, while one-fifth discontinue treatment before completing the recommended course. Siggy can prescribe medications, excluding controlled substances, and clinicians can oversee medication tapering when patients are ready.
